subject: CardinalPay performance gating: proposed test windows & evidence exchange
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Howard <alex.howard@cardinalpay.com>; Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cardinalpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CardinalPay performance gating: proposed test windows & evidence exchange

Hi Alex / Maria —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. To keep momentum and make the onboarding acceptance deterministic, we propose a short, focused test window next week where Redwood runs two load passes and CardinalPay runs parallel client-side verification.

High-level ask from Redwood:
- Provide a stable API endpoint for the test window (auth token + sample payloads)
- Share any rate-limit or caching behavior we should be aware of
- Provide a sample dataset for the functional payloads (or confirm we should use our synthetic variants)

Proposed windows (PDT):
- Wed 2026-07-01 09:00–11:00 (throughput pass)
- Thu 2026-07-02 14:00–15:30 (tail latency + concurrency verification)

Target acceptance gates we intend to measure (internal Redwood gating):
- Sustained throughput: 250 req/s (95th percentile of total successful token responses)
- 95th percentile latency: <= 200 ms
- 99th percentile tail latency: <= 800 ms
- No more than 0.5% error rate at target throughput

I attached a lightweight load plan for CardinalPay to review (cardinalpay_load_plan_v1.xlsx). Monica will be the point for the run execution and result artifacts. Ben will coordinate procurement/contract follow-ups if anything changes.

Please confirm the test windows and whether you want Redwood to use your sample payloads or our synthetic set. Also let us know where to upload run artifacts (drive link or ticket).

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Attachments: cardinalpay_load_plan_v1.xlsx
From: Alex Howard <alex.howard@cardinalpay.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cardinalpay.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CardinalPay performance gating: proposed test windows & evidence exchange

Sean —

Thanks, that timeline works for us. A few clarifying questions before the runs:
1) For the sustained throughput target, is 250 req/s measured at the request-per-second at the HTTP layer or at token-level generation throughput? We need to align our client-side generators.
2) Do you simulate KV cache hits/misses? Our production traffic has a high cache-hit rate (~60%) for repeated prompts.
3) On artifacts: we prefer the run logs to be uploaded to our S3 bucket; procurement will need a signed evidence pack after acceptance.

We will provide a stable endpoint and a scoped dataset by EOD today. Maria (QA) will coordinate our internal verification — she has some sample traces attached that demonstrate our baseline during low-traffic hours.

— Alex
Alex Howard
Head of Engineering, CardinalPay
alex.howard@cardinalpay.com

Attachments: baseline_traces_june.log (referenced inline)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Howard <alex.howard@cardinalpay.com>; Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cardinalpay.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CardinalPay performance gating: proposed test windows & evidence exchange

Alex, thanks — quick answers and a thin runbook overview: 

1) Measurement: Redwood will report both HTTP-level request/sec (RPS) and token-level throughput; our acceptance gates will be evaluated primarily on end-to-end latency and success rate at the requested RPS. We'll include per-token CPU/GPU utilization snapshots in the artifact bundle.

2) Caching: We will run two variants: one with a synthetic cache-hit profile (60% hits) to mimic your production pattern and one cold-cache run. Please indicate if you want us to use your real KV endpoint or our synthetic cache stubbing.

3) Artifacts & evidence: We will produce a single artifact bundle per run containing: request logs, server-side latency histograms, sample traces, and a pass/fail verdict with raw CSVs. If you prefer S3 ingestion, provide an upload role; otherwise we will share a secured Drive folder.

Quick target recap (for CardinalPay acceptance):
- Sustained target: 250 RPS (HTTP) with <0.5% error rate
- P95 latency <= 200 ms (end-to-end)
- P99 latency <= 800 ms
- Stability: no intermittent server-side OOMs or degraded throughput during a 10-minute sliding window at target load

Link to our artifact template & run checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-example-cardinalpay-performance

I'll plan to own the execution window and upload the artifacts to the Drive folder immediately after each run. If procurement needs a sealed evidence pack, Ben can coordinate the signed bundle.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_throughput_targets.pdf
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cardinalpay.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Alex Howard <alex.howard@cardinalpay.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 14:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CardinalPay performance gating: proposed test windows & evidence exchange

Monica / Sean —

Appreciate the clarifications. We confirmed the endpoint and uploaded a small set of traces and a sample payload set to the S3 path below. For the cache behavior, please use our real KV endpoint during the production-like run on Thu.

S3 upload: s3://cardinalpay-ci/perf-tests/2026-07-02/

We ran a quick internal sweep this morning against the endpoint at ~150 RPS and saw P95 ~180ms, P99 ~610ms. I attached a short log excerpt (latency_sample_traces_0702.log). Our QA will be online during both windows to capture client-side metrics.

Two small asks:
- Can Redwood include GPU duty-cycle snapshots (1s granularity) in the artifact bundle? Those are helpful for our capacity team.
- If Redwood sees any request-level 5xx spikes, please flag immediately in Slack and hold the run until we investigate.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
QA Lead, CardinalPay
maria.lopez@cardinalpay.com

Attachments: latency_sample_traces_0702.log
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Howard <alex.howard@cardinalpay.com>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@cardinalpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CardinalPay performance gating: proposed test windows & evidence exchange

Alex / Maria —

Thanks for running the preliminary checks and for the artifacts. Final notes and next actions after the two runs: 

- Redwood will run the scheduled throughput pass on 2026-07-01 and the tail-latency pass on 2026-07-02 as planned. We will upload the artifact bundles to the shared Drive folder and notify your QA channel when each bundle is available.
- Deliverables per run: CSV of request-level latencies, histogram PNGs, GPU utilization snapshots, a short narrative summary (pass/fail + notable observations).
- If run artifacts show pass on the acceptance gates, Procurement can sign the acceptance certificate and we will move the account to dedicated capacity provisioning. Ben: please prepare the acceptance certificate template for CardinalPay (I copied you).

Open items:
- Alex: confirm whether procurement prefers a signed PDF evidence pack or a DocuSign flow for the acceptance certificate.
- Maria: please confirm S3 upload role by EOD tomorrow; if not available, we will use the Drive folder and provide an MD5 manifest for traceability.

Thanks again — Monica will coordinate execution, and I’ll pull the pass/fail summary into the deal in HubSpot once we have artifacts.

Regards,
Sean
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Attachments: none
